method: top-1 and top-5 accuracy of `bitcode search <root> "<description>"` (the same `SemanticGraph::semantic_search` that backs `search_code` and `get_source --intent` over MCP) against a pinned corpus of (natural-language description, expected semantic path) pairs drawn from real nodes in this repository, run at a fixed commit
motivation: `find_definition` with an exact symbol name works well, but `get_source --intent` and `search_code`/`bitcode search` -- the common case, since an agent usually has a description and not an exact semantic path -- return irrelevant nodes. Two reproductions: `get_source` with intent "the function that builds the MCP discover response" returns unrelated functions (aether-debugger's `Program::function`, aether-app's `render_function`) instead of `mcp::discover_result`; `bitcode search . "static list of MCP tool definitions with names and schemas"` scores every hit 0.07-0.09, indistinguishable from noise. Reading `crates/aether-graph/src/similarity.rs` confirms `semantic_search` is plain Jaccard over an unweighted token set built from `{name} {source}`, with no down-weighting of common tokens (e.g. "function", which appears in dozens of node bodies via `NodeKind::Function`) and no boost for a token matching the node's own name or path. Separately, `semantic_search` only ever considers `NodeKind::Function` nodes -- the `Tool` struct that is literally "the MCP tool definitions with names and schemas" (fields `name`, `description`, `schema`) is a `NodeKind::Type` node and was never a candidate answer, which is a real, independently-confirmed gap and not just a scoring artifact.

corpus.description: the function that builds the MCP discover response
static list of MCP tool definitions with names and schemas
corpus.note: required reproduction 2 from the task; the `TOOLS` static itself is not a graph node at all (no Const/Static NodeKind exists), so the `Tool` struct -- a NodeKind::Type node whose fields are literally `name`, `description`, `schema` -- is the closest node a competent human could expect and the reason semantic_search's Function-only scope had to change, not just its weighting

threshold.rationale: Set before measuring the fixed implementation (the unweighted-Jaccard baseline is expected to score far below this -- it is reported for contrast but not gated). 0.75/0.90 is deliberately short of 1.0: some corpus descriptions (e.g. the Anthropic `complete` stub, or `resolve`'s partial-name matching) paraphrase intent in words that do not appear verbatim in the node's name, path, or body, and a token-overlap method -- even IDF-weighted with a name/path boost -- is not expected to win every one of those. The two required reproductions are corpus entries like any other, not a separate gate; the pass bar treats them as ordinary evidence.

reported_but_not_gated: baseline (pre-fix) top-1 and top-5 accuracy of the unweighted-Jaccard implementation, for contrast
per-item results: description, expected_path, ranked hits returned, rank of the expected path if present
